prompt.v: A school play sells adult tickets for $16, student tickets for $9 and child tickets for $5. One night it sold 130 tickets and took in $1,344. It sold three times as many student tickets as child tickets. How many of each did it sell? Give (a, s, c): adult, student, child.

problems.text: tickets: prices 16 9 5; 130 sold; 1344 taken; students 3 times children
problems.explain: a + s + c = 130, 16a + 9s + 5c = 1344, and s = 3c. Put s = 3c into both: a + 4c = 130 and 16a + 32c = 1344. The first gives a = 130 − 4c; then 16(130 − 4c) + 32c = 1344, so 2080 − 32c = 1344 and c = 23. Then s = 69 and a = 38. So (a, s, c) = (38, 69, 23).
